text: Beautiful resort, the pool area is quite literally a stunning oasis just outside of Chiang Mai - 15 minutes down the road. Fred the owner aka Posture Fred is what I am going to call him is an absolute legend (ask him about the importance of posture!) . Great knowledge of the area, welcoming and a good laugh. They have an amazing massage clinic on site run by Dr Nooy who is an expert in holistic treatments. Really lucky to find places like this in Chiang Mai.

Staff: They were friendly, helpful by going the extra mile to make us comfortable and meeting our needs. The owner (who was always around) spoke fluent Thai, German and English (and maybe other languages as well) and we could not ask for …

Highly recommended the actives such as the mini golf or massage healing centre. The pool is also amazing!! The place to stay if you are in chiang mai!!

We stayed in this beautiful Resort for two nights. |We needed an early check-in, which was no problem. |The owner is swiss, is fluent in german, english and thai. He and his staff were very welcoming and they are willing to do whatever it …

We were pleasantly surprised to find a spacious Jacuzzi in our room. The pool and pool area were clean, peaceful and surrounded by mature trees. We didn't get to play the mini golf but really enjoyed the peaceful space this property …

It's an excellent place for comfort and privacy, very quiet in a nice ambiance. The owner and the people that work there do everything to make you feel good and are there for advice and any questions. The Thai and the Swiss dishes in the restaurant ware good and tasteful. Pity we did not stay long enough to taste more dishes. The mini.golf meets international competition standards. It's not to far from Chiang Mai.

The food was good but nothing we ordered stuck out as "must come back for" dish. We had the Grilled ham and cheese, Club sandwich, Ham Baguette, Tuna sandwich, Tom Yum soup, Sweet and Sour chicken. The food came out quickly and largely together. There is also a giant map posted in the dining room and a good amount of tourists information available. After lunch we played goofy golf and that made the experience excellent. Golf took about an hour for all 8 of us to play 18 holes and was only about 80 baht each. Great family fun outing.

18 holes. Fairly easy but I wish some of the entrance / tunnels were a bit wider otherwise great course...there are tunnels jumps obstacles and humps. Lots of fun.

One round is 100B or 80B for kids. We were able to drink beer while on the course too.

Afterwards we enjoyed the glass noodle salad and pad see ew noodles in the restaurant.  Very nice.

We will be back for sure. If you like mini golf you will enjoy this day out. Five stars.

We came as a group of eight people. Was no problem for them to handle and have a table where we all fit. We also got an air cooler and mosquito coils. Individual orders had been fine and all delivered without problems in a reasonable time. Food tasted fine. It's not a budget place but also not overpriced like other restaurants in resorts do.

Golf is a club-and-ball sport in which players use various clubs to hit balls into a series of holes on a course in as few strokes as possible.

Golf, unlike most ball games, cannot and does not utilize a standardized playing area, and coping with the varied terrains encountered on different courses is a key part of the game. The game at the usual level is played on a course with an arranged progression of 18 holes, though recreational courses can be smaller, often having nine holes. Each hole on the course must contain a teeing ground to start from, and a putting green containing the actual hole or cup 4 1⁄4 inches (11 cm) in diameter. There are other standard forms of terrain in between, such as the fairway, rough (long grass), bunkers (or "sand traps"), and various hazards (water, rocks) but each hole on a course is unique in its specific layout and arrangement.

Golf is played for the lowest number of strokes by an individual, known as stroke play, or the lowest score on the most individual holes in a complete round by an individual or team, known as match play. Stroke play is the most commonly seen format at all levels, but most especially at the elite level.
